verdict: Constellation's revenue rose 23% to $7.5B with Calpine now aboard, but unrealized hedge losses cut GAAP profit to $513M even as adjusted earnings rose by a third.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $7,504M, vs $6,101M a year ago — the Calpine deal closed in January 2026

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $2.67 a year ago — held back by unrealized fair-value losses

kpis.label: Adjusted EPS
kpis.note: vs $1.91 a year ago — the company's preferred operating measure

segments.name: Power sales
segments.note: Electricity sold ($4,959M) plus capacity payments ($396M) — paying Constellation to keep plants available to the grid. From the 10-Q revenue note.

segments.name: Gas & other contract revenue
segments.note: Natural gas sales ($327M) and other customer-contract revenue ($161M), largely from the acquired Calpine business.

segments.name: Other revenue sources
segments.note: Revenue outside customer contracts — mainly mark-to-market moves on power hedges and similar items. Volatile by nature, and the reason GAAP profit swings.

opex.name: Operations & maintenance
opex.note: Running the nuclear, gas and renewables fleet day to day — up 39% YoY with Calpine's plants added.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of power plants and equipment over their lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Taxes other than income
opex.note: Property and similar taxes — separate from income tax, which sits below.

otherDetail: Other income added $328M in total counting the $6M equity line: $603M of other income (largely nuclear decommissioning trust gains) and a $2M gain on asset sales, minus $283M of net interest expense, plus $6M of income from unconsolidated affiliates.
oneTimers: Unrealized losses on fair-value adjustments (hedges and related items) cost $340M after tax in the quarter — the biggest single reason GAAP EPS ($1.42) sits far below adjusted operating EPS ($2.55).

Amortization of commodity contracts acquired with Calpine cost $149M after tax, and Calpine merger and integration costs were $84M after tax; decommissioning-related gains added $221M after tax the other way. Adjusted operating earnings were $920M in total.
footerNote: Adaptation: reported operating income of $580M includes a $2M gain on asset sales; here that gain is counted in other income, so operating income shows as $578M. Total net income was $508M; $513M was attributable to common shareholders because noncontrolling interests absorbed a $5M loss. Constellation had not yet reported Q3 2026 when this page was built, so Q2 2026 is its latest quarter.

takeaways.title: Calpine transformed the scale
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 23% to $7.5B. The acquired Calpine fleet supplied 27,642 of 89,815 total GWh sold in the quarter, on top of 44,160 GWh of nuclear generation.

takeaways.title: Big customers are signing long deals
takeaways.text: Constellation signed another 920 MW of 15–20-year power purchase agreements for nuclear power starting 2029–2032, and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $11.50–$12.50.

takeaways.title: GAAP profit is the noisy number
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS fell to $1.42 from $2.67 on $340M of after-tax unrealized fair-value losses and Calpine deal costs — while adjusted operating EPS rose 34% to $2.55. Watch both: the adjustments recur every quarter.
